idiom_name: Mutex<HashMap<K, V>> or OnceLock for a single computed value
implementation_notes: std has no cache: the pattern starts as HashMap<K, V> behind a Mutex/RwLock, or OnceLock for one value computed at most once, with eviction and TTL written by hand because nothing in std tracks recency or expiry. The borrow checker shapes the design - values in a shared cache must be owned or Arc-shared and effectively immutable, so handing out references across a possible eviction does not compile; return clones or Arc handles instead. Weak<T> plus upgrade() is how Rust expresses GC-owned cache keys. Reach for the lru or moka crate once a real bound, TTL or lock-free read path is needed.
pitfalls: Holding the MutexGuard while calling the loader serializes every lookup and deadlocks if the loader re-enters the cache - std's Mutex is not reentrant.
Returning references into the map is impossible; cloning every hit is the naive workaround (wrap large values in Arc<str>/Arc<Vec<_>> to make it cheap).
Weak<T> keys need upgrade() and a separate strong owner, or entries are dropped as soon as the last strong reference goes away.
std's HashMap has no TTL: expired entries must be swept by the caller, and the sweep needs the same lock.

variants.name: moka concurrent cache with TTL and weigher (crate)
variants.implementation_notes: moka is the concurrent-cache crate: Cache::builder().max_capacity(n).time_to_live(...).time_to_idle(...).weigher(...).build() gives a lock-free read path with TinyLFU admission and TTL/TTI expiry, and moka::future::Cache offers the same API under async/await. Because the cache is internally synchronized and get returns a clone, it sidesteps the Mutex-per-lookup cost of the hand-rolled variant; the price is an extra dependency and value cloning. Choose it for shared caches with real eviction pressure or expiry requirements; the lru crate remains the minimal alternative for a plain bounded LRU.
pitfalls: get returns a clone, so every hit clones the value - store Arc<T> or small Copy types, or the cache becomes the bottleneck.
Maintenance (capacity enforcement, expiry) is amortised in background tasks: the cache can briefly exceed max_capacity unless run_pending_tasks() is forced.
Async cache calls must not be made while holding another lock, and blocking loaders inside future::Cache::get_with starve the executor.
